title: At the bottom of the well, a promise reached him.
subtitle: Comfort sent in the darkest moment

row.title: a promise
sub: you will tell them one day

then: The brothers {trap}all agreed{/trap} and lowered Yusuf into the well, then cut the rope. Ibn Kathir notes that in that distress Allah revealed to him: {reward}you will one day tell them of this, while they do not recognize you.{/reward} Relief was sent inside the hardship.
now: The hospital corridor at 3 a.m. The empty flat after the divorce. The phone that has not rung since the layoff. {idea}This verse says comfort can reach you there,{/idea} not only after you climb out.
old: When I am at the bottom, Allah feels far away.
new: The bottom of the well is exactly where the promise was sent.
try: In your next hard moment, say quietly: Allah sees this, and a way out is coming.

title: They came home at night, weeping.
subtitle: Tears used as part of the plan
then: After the well, the brothers returned {trap}in the darkness of the night, crying and showing sorrow.{/trap} The night and the tears were both part of the story they had agreed to tell.
now: Someone cries during an argument and the conversation ends there. Sometimes it is real pain. Sometimes {trap}it is a way to stop the questions.{/trap} And sometimes the one doing it is you.
old: If they are crying, they must be telling the truth.
new: Tears show feeling, not always truth, so I look gently at what was done.
try: If you feel tears rising to end an argument, pause and say the honest sentence first.

title: A wolf ate him, and you will not believe us anyway.
subtitle: Using his own fear as their excuse
then: They said they went racing and left Yusuf by their belongings, and {trap}a wolf devoured him, exactly what Yaqub had feared.{/trap} Then they added that he would not believe them even if they were truthful, {trap}trying to blunt his doubt before it came.{/trap}
now: You know your partner's worst worry, your parent's soft spot, your boss's pet fear. In a tight spot it is tempting to {trap}use it as the excuse,{/trap} because it will sound believable. That is turning someone's trust into a tool.
old: If the excuse matches what they already feared, it is harmless.
new: Using someone's own fear to cover my lie wounds them twice.
try: Next time you need an excuse, give the true reason instead, even if it is smaller.

title: False blood on an untorn shirt. Beautiful patience.
subtitle: Seeing through a lie and choosing patience
then: They brought Yusuf's shirt stained with a sheep's blood, but {trap}forgot to tear it.{/trap} Yaqub said their souls had made up a tale. He chose {idea}patience most fitting,{/idea} seeking Allah's help against what they described.
now: You know you are being lied to. The receipt does not match, the story has holes. You could explode, or collapse. {idea}Yaqub named the lie and then turned to Allah{/idea} instead of turning on everyone.
old: When I know I have been wronged, patience means letting them get away with it.
new: I can see the truth clearly and still choose patience, leaning on Allah.
try: Say Allahul mustaan, Allah is the one whose help is sought, the next time you are wronged.

title: A bucket comes down. Good news, here is a boy.
subtitle: Rescue and sale in the same moment
then: After about three days, a caravan sent its water drawer, and {reward}Yusuf held on to the bucket.{/reward} He was then hidden as merchandise. Ibn Kathir says {idea}Allah knew what they did and could have stopped it,{/idea} but by His wisdom let His decree unfold, a reminder to the Prophet ﷺ facing his own people.
now: The rescue does not look like a rescue. You get out of a bad job straight into a worse contract. {idea}Allah sees every step,{/idea} even the ones that feel like going from one trap into another.
old: If this rescue led to something worse, Allah was not watching.
new: Allah knew every hand involved, and the story was still moving toward good.
try: Write down one hard turn in your life that later led somewhere good.

title: Sold for a few coins by those who saw nothing in him.
subtitle: The price people put on you is not your worth
then: Ibn Abbas and others said the brothers sold him. Ibn Masud put the price at twenty dirhams, {trap}split two each.{/trap} Ad-Dahhak said they valued him so little {idea}because they had no knowledge of his rank with Allah.{/idea}
now: The interview where they barely looked up. The relative who calls you the disappointment. The salary offer that felt like an insult. {idea}People price you by what they can see.{/idea} Allah sees the rest.
old: If people treat me as worth little, maybe I am.
new: My worth is set by Allah, not by those who cannot see it.
try: Write down one quality Allah gave you that nobody around you has noticed yet.

title: Make his stay honorable. Allah prevails in His affair.
subtitle: From a slave market into a minister's house
then: The man who bought Yusuf was the Aziz, minister of Egypt. Ibn Masud counted him among {reward}three people with the most insight.{/reward} Just as Allah saved Yusuf from his brothers, He settled him in Egypt. {idea}Allah has full control over His affairs.{/idea}
now: You were moved to a new city for a job you did not choose, or a new school after a family split. It feels random. {idea}Allah's plan can run through other people's ordinary decisions,{/idea} a boss, a landlord, a teacher who decided to be kind.
old: My life is shaped by whoever happens to have power over me.
new: Allah prevails over His affair, even through people who do not know it.
try: Thank one person today who made your stay somewhere easier, even in a small way.

title: When he grew up, he was given wisdom and knowledge.
subtitle: Doing good, and being rewarded with understanding
then: Yusuf grew up in a stranger's house, far from his family. When he reached maturity, Allah gave him {reward}wisdom and knowledge, the prophethood.{/reward} Ibn Kathir says this was {idea}because he used to do good in obedience to Allah.{/idea}
now: You are in a place you did not choose: a junior job, a foreign country, a house that is not home. You keep being decent anyway. {idea}That quiet goodness is what this verse says gets rewarded,{/idea} often with understanding.
old: Being good where no one notices is a waste.
new: Doing good in a hard place is how Allah prepares and rewards a person.
try: Do one good thing today at work or school that nobody will see or thank you for.

title: Doors closed, she called. He said, I seek refuge in Allah.
subtitle: Saying no when everything is set up for yes
then: The wife of the Aziz, in whose house he lived, {trap}closed the doors and called him to herself.{/trap} His first words were {idea}I seek refuge in Allah.{/idea} Then he said her husband had treated him well and he would never betray him.
now: A private message late at night. A hotel on a work trip. A door that locks and a phone that nobody checks. {idea}The first move is to turn to Allah,{/idea} the second is to remember who trusts you.
old: No one would ever know, so it would not really hurt anyone.
new: Allah knows, and the people who trust me matter even when they cannot see.
try: Pick a short phrase, like audhu billah, to say the moment temptation knocks.

title: A thought crossed his mind. A proof from his Lord stopped it.
subtitle: Turning away from a sin you were drawn to
then: Al-Baghawi explained the verse as {trap}a thought crossing the mind.{/trap} He cited the hadith that a bad deed intended but left for Allah's sake {reward}is written as a good deed.{/reward} At-Tabari said the proof Yusuf saw is best left vague, as Allah left it.
now: The pull is real. You did not choose to feel it. The screen is open, the opportunity is right there. {idea}Feeling drawn is not the failure.{/idea} Turning away for Allah is the win.
old: If I even felt drawn to it, I am already as bad as if I did it.
new: Being tempted is human, and walking away for Allah is counted as good.
try: Next time you resist something, tell Allah quietly: I left this for You.

title: It was she who sought me. Then a witness spoke.
subtitle: Speaking the truth plainly when accused
then: Accused at the door, Yusuf {idea}did not stand idle but declared the truth.{/idea} Then a witness from her household proposed a test: look at where the shirt was torn. Scholars differed on whether the witness was a grown man or a baby in the cradle.
now: You are blamed in the office for a mistake that was not yours. Silence feels safer, shouting feels fair. {idea}Yusuf said one plain, true sentence{/idea} and let the evidence do the rest.
old: If I am falsely accused, either stay quiet or fight hard.
new: I can calmly say what happened and trust the truth to show itself.
try: If you are blamed unfairly this week, write one calm, factual sentence before replying.

title: Torn from the back means he was running away.
subtitle: Evidence that speaks for the innocent
then: The witness reasoned: if he was fleeing and she pulled him back, {idea}the shirt would tear from behind.{/idea} The same object the brothers once used for a lie, a shirt, {reward}now spoke for his innocence.{/reward}
now: Your word against someone with more power: the manager, the older relative, the popular kid. It feels hopeless. {idea}Truth leaves traces{/idea} — a timestamp, a message, a small detail — and Allah can bring them to light.
old: When it is my word against a powerful person, the truth does not matter.
new: Truth leaves its marks, and Allah can make them speak for me.
try: Keep a short, honest record of any situation where you feel unfairly treated.
